result:
Understood, the content is settled. One quick decision on how it gets built, and then I'll write it up.

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my recommendation).** Batches, sacks and bottling runs go in as a new section of the Flask app you already run, with new tables in the same SQLite database on the Pi. There's still one thing to run, back up and update, and it follows patterns the code already uses.
*Trade-off:* the taproom tabs and brewing records depend on each other. A bad update to one can take down both, and a corrupted database file loses both.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** It's built the same way but has its own database file and its own address. A problem on brew day can't touch the bar tabs, and the other way round.
*Trade-off:* you'd have two apps to start, update and back up, and some setup would be duplicated.

Either way, sack scanning would use a plain USB barcode scanner. It types the lot number into the page as if it were a keyboard, so it needs no special drivers. The labels would go through your existing printer.

I'm recommending option 1 because you have one Pi and one person maintaining it. Option 1 also adds the least to look after. Your traceability records would sit in the same backup as everything else. That raises one thing I'll put in the design: how the Pi gets backed up, because a lost database would mean lost traceability.

Given the scale, I'll treat this as a full design document saved with the project. Before I give it to you, a reviewer will read it as if they were going to build from it, and I may come back once with a few questions.

Should I build on the taproom app, or keep it separate?
